extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements from the MPEP governing who may be an applicant, how applicant identity is shown or changed, title and fee requirements, page/claim counting rules, and fee payment/ refund treatment for U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence of ownership when applicant is assignee/obligated assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is the assignee or a person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign the invention, documentary evidence of ownership (e.g., assignment for an assignee, employment agreement for a person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign the invention) should be recorded as provided for in part 3 of this chapter no later than the date the issue fee is paid in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record such documentary evidence in accordance with 37 CFR part 3; recording must be done no later than payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements for applicant showing sufficient proprietary interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter, such applicant must submit a petition including: (i) the fee set forth in § 1.17(g); (ii) a showing that such person has sufficient proprietary interest in the matter; and (iii) a statement that making the application for patent by a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter on behalf of and as agent for the inventor is appropriate to preserve the rights of the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 409.05 for discussion of evidence necessary to show sufficient proprietary interest. The Office may publish notice of the filing in the Official Gazette (37 CFR 1.46(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application data sheet requirement for corrections/updates to applicant name
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of the applicant under this section must include an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the correct or updated name of the applicant in the applicant information section (§ 1.76(b)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected ADS must identify changed information with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for removals as required by § 1.76(c)(2). A change recorded pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 16(1)(ii) will be effective for nonprovisional international design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in applicant must comply with ADS and ownership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to change the applicant under this section after an original applicant has been specified must include an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the applicant in the applicant information section and comply with §§ 3.71 and 3.73 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to change applicant must be supported by the ownership/authority showings required in 37 CFR 3.71/3.73 and should be filed no later than payment of the issue fee; cannot be filed after patent issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirement by actual inventor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the whole or a part interest in the invention or in the patent to be issued is assigned or obligated to be assigned, an oath or declaration must be executed by the actual inventor or each actual joint inventor, except as provided for in § 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.64 concerning execution of a substitute statement by an assignee, obligated assignee, or person showing sufficient proprietary interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent issuance to real party in interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is granted on an application filed under this section by a person other than the inventor, the patent shall be granted to the real party in interest. Where a real party in interest has filed an application under 37 CFR 1.46, the applicant shall notify the Office of any change in the real party in interest no later than payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to notify by issue-fee date will be treated as indication of no change. Identification of real party in interest (e.g., box 3 of PTOL-85B) does not change applicant of record unless a proper request to change applicant under 1.46 is timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'applicant' (37 CFR 1.42/1.43/1.45/1.46 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'applicant' refers to the inventor or all joint inventors, or to the person applying for a patent as provided in 37 CFR 1.43, 1.45, or 1.46. For applications under 37 CFR 1.46, 'applicant' refers to the assignee, the person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign, or the person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter who is applying under 1.46 and not the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fewer than all joint inventors apply under 1.45, 'the applicant' means the joint inventors who are applying without the omitted inventor(s). See MPEP §§ 409.01–409.03 for related rules (deceased/incapacitated inventors, applications by another).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors must apply jointly and execute oaths (37 CFR 1.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint inventors must apply for a patent jointly and each joint inventor must make the inventor’s oath or declaration required by 37 CFR 1.63, except as provided for in 37 CFR 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors may be joint even if they did not physically work together, made unequal contributions, or did not contribute to every claim; each named inventor must have made a contribution to at least one claim (nonprovisional) or to the provisional disclosure (provisional). If a joint inventor refuses to join or cannot be found after diligent effort, the other joint inventor(s) may apply on behalf of the omitted inventor (see 35 U.S.C. 116 and MPEP § 409.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for applications filed by assignee or proprietary-interest party (37 CFR 1.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 is made by a person other than the inventor under 37 CFR 1.46(a), the application must contain an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying in the applicant information section the assignee, obligated assignee, or person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying the party in the ADS is not a filing-date requirement, but delay in naming the applicant may require a request under 1.46(c) and compliance with 3.71/3.73. If assignee is not owner of entire interest, the assignee must be named together with other owning parties; all owners must act as a composite entity before the Office (see MPEP § 301 and 3.71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of applicant — default and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no applicant is identified, the Office will, by default, consider the inventor to be the applicant. Any request to change the applicant must include an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying the applicant and must comply with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New applicant must establish ownership under 3.71(b) and 3.73. A request to change applicant under 1.46(c)(2) should not be filed after the patent has issued because it cannot be granted then.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction/update of applicant name and typographical errors (timing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a minor typographical error in a 37 CFR 1.46 applicant’s name is detected prior to payment of the issue fee, a request under 1.46(c)(1) should be filed promptly and no later than payment of the issue fee, with an ADS specifying the correct name and appropriate markings; neither a fee nor a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(c) is required. If the error is not detected until after payment of the issue fee, the application must be withdrawn from issue or a certificate of correction must be filed with appropriate petitions or RCE/CPA as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For entity name changes (e.g., LLC to Inc.) follow same 1.46(c)(1) timing and ADS marking rules; applicant may optionally submit a statement under 3.73(c) referencing the name-change document. Deletion of a party incorrectly named as applicant cannot be handled under 1.46(c)(1); file a petition under 1.182 with the petition fee (1.17(f)) plus ADS and explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention requirements (37 CFR 1.72)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention may not exceed 500 characters in length and must be as short and specific as possible. The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive and should contain fewer than 500 characters. The title should be placed at the top of the first page of the specification unless supplied in an application data sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain words (e.g., 'A', 'An', 'The', 'New', 'Improved', 'Design', 'Ornamental', etc.) are not considered part of the title and should not be included at the beginning. If the title is not descriptive of the claimed invention, the examiner should require substitution of a new title (form paragraphs 6.11/6.11.01). Examiner may change title at allowance by examiner’s amendment (see MPEP § 1302.04(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing, search, and examination fees — timing and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the following fees are required: basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a),(b),(c) or (e)); search fee (37 CFR 1.16(k),(l),(m), or (n)); examination fee (37 CFR 1.16(o),(p),(q), or (r)); application size fee if applicable (37 CFR 1.16(s)); excess claims fees (37 CFR 1.16(h),(i),(j)) if applicable; and non-electronic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(t)) if applicable. The basic filing, search and examination fees are due on filing but may be paid later if paid within the time set in 37 CFR 1.53(f) and include any surcharge required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications have a basic filing fee under 37 CFR 1.16(d) due on filing but may be paid later per 1.53(g) with surcharge. International/national stage fees have separate rules (see 1.492 and MPEP § 1893.01(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee rules (37 CFR 1.16(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application size fee applies when the specification (including claims) and drawings of an application, excluding certain sequence listings or computer program listings filed in compliance with rules, exceed 100 sheets of paper; the fee applies for each additional 50 sheets or fraction thereof over 100 sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments present on the filing date count toward the page total; the Office recommends against filing substitute specifications or multiple sets of drawings at initial filing. For applications submitted on electronic medium other than EFS-Web, each 3 kilobytes of content counts as a sheet. For applications submitted via EFS-Web, the paper-equivalent is considered 75% of the number of sheets when rendered by the Office. Sequence listings/computer program listings submitted as ASCII text via EFS-Web may be excluded; PDF/TIFF listings/drawings are not excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fee rules (37 CFR 1.16(h),(i),(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fee applies for each independent claim in excess of three and for each claim (independent or dependent) in excess of twenty; fees also apply to reissue applications. Fees for a proper multiple dependent claim are calculated based on the number of claims to which it refers (37 CFR 1.75(c)); separate fees are required for each application containing a proper multiple dependent claim (37 CFR 1.16(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional applications filed without claims, if more than three independent claims, more than twenty total claims, or a multiple dependent claim are presented, the excess claims fee is due when such claims are presented. Amendments that affect claims require payment of additional fees for claims in excess of previously paid amounts; amendments without full additional fee will not be entered or will be treated as non-responsive to Office action. Cancellation of claims may reduce counted claims but no refund is made for claims already paid for (see MPEP § 607.02 for refund policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-electronic filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional fee of $400 ($200 for a small entity) shall be established for each application for an original patent (except design, plant, or provisional applications) not filed by electronic means (see 37 CFR 1.16(t)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed on/after November 15, 2011 not filed via the USPTO electronic filing system (EFS-Web). See 37 CFR 1.445(a)(1)(ii) for related rules for international applications filed with the USPTO as receiving Office on/after November 15, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order for applying insufficient payments when applicant does not specify
rubrics_metrics.description: When a payment submitted for the fees due on filing in a nonprovisional application is insufficient and applicant has not specified the fees to which payment should be applied, the Office will apply the payment in the following order until expended: (1) basic filing fee; (2) non-electronic filing fee; (3) application size fee; (4) late filing surcharge; (5) processing fee for application filed in a language other than English; (6) search fee; (7) examination fee; (8) excess claims fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisional applications, the Office will apply insufficient payment in this order: (1) basic filing fee; (2) application size fee; (3) late filing surcharge. See also MPEP § 509.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit account authorization treatment for 'filing fee' charges
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will treat a deposit account authorization to charge 'the filing fee' as an authorization to charge the applicable fees under 37 CFR 1.16 (the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, any excess claims fee, and any application size fee) to the deposit account. A deposit account authorization to charge 'the basic filing fee' will be treated as authorization to charge the applicable basic filing, search, and examination fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any deposit account authorization to charge the filing fee but not the search or examination fee must specifically limit the authorization by reference to the applicable paragraphs of 37 CFR 1.16. See MPEP § 509.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and returnability of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or any amount paid in excess of that required. See 37 U.S.C. 42 and 37 CFR 1.26 (Refunds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 607.02 and 37 CFR 1.26 for procedures and circumstances for refunds.
